get.description:
This endpoint retrieves the list of fixtures for a given sport.

### Important information 
- Sportradar has a database of fixtures across all major sports and tournaments. Use this API to retrieve Sportradar Fixture IDs. You can then map these to your own internal Fixture IDs to ensure odds messages are sent for the correct fixture/match/event. 
- The response includes detailed fixture information with Sportradar-generated IDs
- Supports filtering by tournament:
  - Use the `tournament.name` parameter to filter fixtures by tournament name.
- Supports filtering by date range:
  - The `from_date` should be not older than 30 days from the current date.
  - The range should be less than 7 days.
  - The `from_date` should be earlier than the `to_date`
  - Both dates should be in ISO format (e.g., 2023-01-01)

post.description:
This endpoint is used to send a heartbeat message to maintain an active connection for a particular sport event, identified by its unique id.

## Important information
### LIVE only
Heartbeat is required only during `LIVE` operation.
`PRE_MATCH` does NOT require heartbeat.

### Timing rule 
During a sport event, Sportradar must receive **either an Odds update or a Heartbeat** at least once every **5 seconds** for the sport event.

- If you are sending Odds updates at least every 5 seconds, you do not need heartbeat.
- If you have **no Odds message to send within 5 seconds**, send a Heartbeat to keep the session active.

#### Do not send heartbeats more frequently than every 5 seconds
Sending heartbeats more frequently may lead to rate limiting and issues.

### Timeout behavior and deactivation
Heartbeat messages are sport-event-specific (not market-specific). A Heartbeat keeps **all open markets** active for that sport event.

If no Odds/Heartbeat message is received within the required timeframe, **all open markets may be automatically deactivated**, and you will receive a notification via the registered `market_deactivation` webhook. 

(To understand how markets are deactivated, please refer to Webhook Subscription → `market_deactivation`).

**You can find examples of such messages in the `examples` tab.**

schema.title: Session.Heartbeat
schema.description:
This message indicates that the source/producer is currently connected to the broker and working properly.
If used, it is recommended that the heartbeat message is sent at least every 10 seconds unless other data is being sent.
If other data is being sent continuously then heartbeats don't need to be sent. Only if there is a gap of more than 10 seconds without data should a heartbeat be sent.
To make implementations easier, producers are free to send heartbeat messages every 10 seconds regardless of when other data is sent, but that is not a requirement.

id.description:
Identifies the message. Producers MUST ensure that source + id is unique for each distinct message.

source.description:
Reference: https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/v1.0.2/cloudevents/spec.md#source-1

Producers MUST ensure that `source` + `id` is unique for each distinct message. In S3P, the `source` property is defined this way:

`/<Producer>/<Integration>[:<Version>]/<Sport>/<CoverageId>/<Instance>`

- Producer - a string assigned by SR to an S3P producer. For internal SR services, the `service-key` must be used, e.g. `compsol`, `ld`, `pet` etc.
- Integration - a string provided by the producer indicating the name of the integration to S3P. This may be the name of the product etc. It should be short and contain no spaces, e.g. `dc`, `igp`, `clsplus`.
- Version - an optional string provided by the producer indicating the version of the integration, e.g. `1.0.1`.
- Sport - a string (defined as part of S3P) giving the name of sport or business domain (betting) for which data is being sent, e.g. `basketball`, `cricket`, `football`, `table-tennis`, `betting`.
- CoverageId - This is the unique identifier of the coverage being provided. If the producer does not internally have a coverageId to include, this field should be set to `1`. If the producer knows a coverageId IS in use, but doesn't know what it is, then this field should be set to `0`.
- Instance - a string provided by the producer giving an instance identifier for the producer of the data. For a producer like CV, this could be a particular server or process identifier, for human entered data this could also be an individual scout identifier. Remember to also include this information in the _coverage_ message.

datacontenttype.description:
Content type of the data value. Must adhere to RFC 2046 format.

Compressed data is ALWAYS sent in the _data_base64_ property. The _data_ property is omitted (https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/v1.0.2/cloudevents/formats/json-format.md).

Data sent in compressed format MUST always be a valid json object.

The _datacontenttype_ header indicates the type of compression being used. The field should be of the form `application/` followed by the type of compression (eg _gzip_). When compressed data is not being sent, the _datacontenttype_ header is optional (defaulting to `application/json`). If you are sending compressed data in the _data_base64_ header then the datacontenttype is REQUIRED.

While this may expand in the future, as of now, the only valid value for this is `application/gzip` with the compression being performed with the gzip algorithm.

subject.description:

- sport_event
- season
- competition
- competitor
- person

`identifier` is the identifier as given by the producer, so something like `sport_event:sr:match:123` is also valid.
For some scenarios, multiple subjects may need to be given. Eg statistics for a competitor in a competition. In these situations a comma separated list of identifiers should be given.

Timestamps related to the data payload have their own properties, and this property only reflects when the message was generated.

See more at https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/v1.0.2/cloudevents/extensions/sequence.md#sequence-1
For Integer sequence types the sequence must be consecutive and begin at 1.

post.description:
This endpoint is used to send odds data for a particular sport event, identified by its unique id. The same endpoint is used for **PRE_MATCH**, **LIVE**, and **COMPETITION_ODDS** messages. ## Important Information ### 1) PRE_MATCH vs LIVE vs COMPETITION_ODDS You send PRE_MATCH, LIVE, and COMPETITION_ODDS through this endpoint, but you must select the correct **product** in the URL and the correct **producer** in the message. | Phase | `{product}` in URL | `producer` in message | |---|---|---| | Pre-match odds | `pre` | `PRE_MATCH` | | Live odds | `liveodds` | `LIVE` | | Competition odds | `codds` | `COMPETITION_ODDS` | #### PRE_MATCH cut-off rule ~~(15 minutes)~~ ~~We enforce a strict 15-minute window right before the sport event start time that separates PRE_MATCH from LIVE updates:~~ ~~- `PRE_MATCH` messages are accepted **until 15 minutes before** the sport event start time.~~ ~~- `LIVE` messages are accepted **15 minutes before** the sport event start time onward.~~ | 🚧 DEPRECATED 🚧 | | --- | | We're in the process of switching to cut-off of 0, i.e. at the scheduled start time.
For more details please see the new pre-match section. | #### What happens if you send the wrong type at the wrong time? Messages outside the allowed window are **not processed** and you will receive a `validation_failure` callback. #### Sport event state expectations Your payload includes `betting_event_state`. This state should reflect the sport event phase: - In `PRE_MATCH`, `sport_event_status` is typically `NOT_STARTED`. Period details (e.g. `period` / `periods`) are omitted. - In `LIVE`, `sport_event_status` is typically `IN_PROGRESS`. Period and clock details are present. ### 2) Rate limit and batching We expect **maximum 1 message per second per sport event** from you If your system is able to generate more than 1 odds update within 1 second, **then you need to collate those updates and send as 1 single message each second** ### 3) Message payload conventions - We expect to receive **true odds** with no margins applied. Our clients have the flexibility to configure their own odds keys (margin) to suit their respective risk profiles. - A message **without `markets`** means that some other information has changed (e.g. `sport_event_status`), while markets have not. - When market has inactive outcome, **do not send** the `odds` field for that outcome. - Avoid sending odds with values near to `1.01`, as for some bookmakers such updates may be ignored. Moreover, some outcomes or markets can be automatically deactivated! - Use `Sportradar's Market Lifecycle` section to find the description of each market status. We expect you to align with our market's definition and status. **You can find examples of such messages in the `examples` tab. Please find the corresponding example to your sport and markets and apply mappings similarly.**

lap.description: The number or the instance of a lap. Used in athletic or motor sports.

leg.description: The number or the instance of a leg. A leg is a single game in the sport of darts.

map.description: The instance of a map. Used in E-sports

max_overs.description: The maximum number of overs in a match. Used in sports in cricket.

minute.description: The number of elapsed minutes in a match

over.description: The number or instance of a over. Used in cricket.

from_over.description: The instance of a over. Used in conjunction with specifier "to_over" to refer to two different overs in a market

to_over.description: The instance of a over. Used in conjunction with specifier "from_over" to refer to two different overs in a market

penalty.description: The number or instance of penalty

period.description: Refers to the number of or an instance of a period in a match. A period is a division of time in a match, in which play occurs.

places.description: Number of places that are paid out with each-way (e/w) terms.

pitch.description: The number or instance of pitch. Used in bat & ball sports.

player1.description: The name of a player in the match. Used in conjunction with "player2", "player3" in markets where multiple players are being identified.

player2.description: The name of a player in the match. Used in conjunction with "player1", "player3" in markets where multiple players are being identified.

player3.description: The name of a player in the match. Used in conjunction with "player2", "player1" in markets where multiple players are being identified.

play.description: The number or instance of play. Used in sports like American Football

possession.description: Refers to an instance of possession. A possession refers to a period where a certain team has control over the ball. Used in sports like Basketball or soccer

qualifying_period.description: Refers to an instance of a qualifying period in a sport. Used in motor sports, a qualifying period refers to various rounds of qualifying which are used to establish the starting grid.

quarter.description: Refers to a period in a match.

retirement.description: Refers to an instance of number of retirement. Used in motor sports, it refers to when a player has to withdraw due to accident or mechanical failure

region.description: Regional scope for the settlement of the market.

round.description: Refers to the number of or an instance of a round. A round is a stage in a competition

server.description: Refers to the player serving for the game. Used in racquet sports.

session.description: Refers to the number of or an instance of a session. A session is a period of play. Used in sports like cricket

stop.description: The number or instance of a stop. Used in motor sports

timeout.description: The number or instance of a timeout.

to_frame.description: The instance of a frame. Used in conjunction with specifier "from_frame" to refer to two different frames in a market

touchdown.description: The number or instance of a touchdown. Used in sports like American Football & Rugby.

turnover.description: The number or instance of a turnover. Used in sports like Basketball, American Football & Rugby.

visit.description: The number or instance of a visit. A single visit or turn to the board gives the player the chance to throw three darts. Used in sports like darts.

variant.description: The variant of the event. Used in markets where set of outcomes is defined by specific variant.

end.description: Refers to the number of or an instance of an end. An end is a stage in a competition in Bowls

frames.description: The number of frames. A frame refers to a single game in the match. Used in context of cue sports like snooker

games.description: This specifier refers to a number of games. Like x games in Tennis

goals.description: The number of goals in a match

group.description: Refers to a group in a tournament.

handicap_including_draw.description: This is handicap used in European handicap markets. The handicap is represented as a score (Ex: 0:1) as opposed to a number.

match_reference.description: This specifier is used to pass the match reference. It is used lo link head-to-head markets (which are setup as separate matches) with the actual event.

innings.description: The number of innings. Used in bat & ball sports like cricket, baseball

matchday.description: Refers to the day in an event.

milestone.description: It represents a significant score in a match. Currently being used in cricket to indicate scores like centuries (100 runs) or half-century (50 runs)

milestone1.description: The specifier represents a significant score in a match. It is used in conjunction with specifier "milestone2" to indicate a pair of scores to be achieved

milestone2.description: The specifier represents a significant score in a match. It is used in conjunction with specifier "milestone1" to indicate a pair of scores to be achieved

points.description: Refers to the number of points in the match.

position.description: Represents the position in a league. A position shows where each team ranks in their conference or division.

run_instance.description: Refers to a specific run in a sport. A run is a passage of play in certain sports like Skiing

runs.description: The number of goals in a match. Runs here refer to the score & is used in games like cricket

score_number.description: The number or instance of a score. This is represented numerically. Used in sports like darts, ice hockey

selected_number.description: This indicates the number that has been selected. Used in context of betting games like lottery.

team.description: Refers to a particular team who are part of a match/event. Currently used in "Formula 1"

terms.description: Each-way fraction that is relevant for calculating the payout.

odds_type.description: This indicates the type of odds being generated by the market. It is used independent of the state of the match, and it helps distinguish versions of the market based on the info about line-up when the market was initiated (pre-match, less info on line-up & live - higher confidence about the line-up)

ups.description: Used in spread betting. This specifier is used to represent the score beyond (ups) a certain threshold

winners.description: Represents the number of winners in a game. Used in sports where multiple teams or individuals are participating in the game.

xth.description: The specifier is being used as a variable to refer to a certain incident in a match. Its currently being used in E-sports, Snooker & Darts.

rally.description: Refers to a specific rally in a sport. A rally is the period during which the ball is in play in sports like Table Tennis.

count.description: Refers to the number of a certain event in a match. For example, the number of assists, shots, etc. in a soccer match.

xup.description: Refers to the number of a certain event in a match. For example, the goal advantage in soccer match.

try.description: The number or instance of a try. This is represented numerically. Used in rugby

course.description: The course this market applies to, carried as a venue identifier.

- IN_PROGRESS - The football sport event has begun and is ongoing (including extra time and penalty shootout when applicable).
- INTERRUPTED - The football sport event has been INTERRUPTED by an exceptional event outside the normal sport flow (e.g. severe weather, crowd disturbance, floodlight failure). The match may resume later.
- ABANDONED - The football sport event has started but has been terminated early and will NOT resume.

sport_event_status.title: Basketball.SportEventStatus
sport_event_status.description:
The state of the sport event.
- NOT_STARTED - The Sport Event hasn't started yet and is intended to be played according to the schedule (e.g. not POSTPONED or DELAYED)
- POSTPONED - The Sport Event has been POSTPONED do a different day. It will not start now. Postponed sport events CAN have changed start date (if postponing is for shorter time, e.g. up to 48 hours) OR result in scheduling another sport event (with separate ID)
- DELAYED - The Sport Event has been temporarily DELAYED, it will be played the same day, but not at the scheduled time. The delay may be minutes or hours. Delayed sport events retain their original planned start time, but will have different actual start time
- PLAYERS_ON_PITCH - The Players have entered the field of play
- PLAYERS_WARMING_UP - The Players have started warming up
- ABOUT_TO_START - The Sport event is about to start. After the players have completed the warm up and the sport event is due to commence in the next few minutes.
- IN_PROGRESS - The Sport event has begun. Note: Any timeouts or period breaks do not affect this status.
- INTERRUPTED - The game has been INTERRUPTED by an unseen event outside the normal sport flow.  eg Loss of power in the venue
- ABANDONED - The game has stopped and will NOT restart
- ENDED - The game has FINISHED (and Overtime has NOT been played) eg the clock is at 0 at the end of the last period
- ENDED_AFTER_OT - The game has FINISHED (and Overtime HAS been played) eg the clock is at 0 at the end of the last overtime period
- CONFIRMED - The game has ended and all data has been confirmed as correct.
- PROTESTED - The team is protesting the result.

sport_event_status.title: Baseball.SportEventStatus
sport_event_status.description:
Lifecycle status of a Baseball sport event. Statuses cover normal progress and exceptional outcomes.
- NOT_STARTED - The baseball sport event hasn't started yet and is intended to be played according to the schedule (e.g. not POSTPONED or DELAYED)
- ABOUT_TO_START - The baseball sport event is expected to start in the next few minutes (lineups/anthem/introductions complete or near complete).
- PLAYERS_ON_COURT - Teams are on the diamond (field of play) and taking positions.
- PLAYERS_WARMING_UP - Pre-game warm-ups are in progress (e.g. bullpen, infield/outfield practice).
- IN_PROGRESS - The baseball sport event is in progress. Note: Between-inning/half-inning breaks and routine stoppages (e.g. pitching changes, mound visits) do not affect this status.
- FINISHED - The baseball sport event has completed normally and a final result is available.
- INTERRUPTED - The baseball sport event has been INTERRUPTED by an unseen event outside the normal sport flow (e.g. Loss of power in the venue).
- RETIRED - The baseball sport event ended due to a competitor retiring during play.
- DEFAULTED - The baseball sport event was awarded to one competitor due to the other competitor declared the loser due to a rules/eligibility/administrative breach.
- DELAYED - The start of the baseball sport event is delayed (e.g. weather-related) but the game is still expected to begin or resume.
- ABANDONED - The baseball sport event has stopped and will NOT be continued.
- WALKOVER - The baseball sport event was awarded to one competitor due to the other competitor not participating.
- POSTPONED - The baseball sport event has been POSTPONED do a different day. It will not start now.
- SUSPENDED - The baseball sport event started but has been SUSPENDED and is scheduled to be resumed later from the point of interruption.
- CANCELLED - The baseball sport event has been cancelled and will not be played.

sport_event_status.title: EBasketball.SportEventStatus
sport_event_status.description:
The state of the sport event.
- NOT_STARTED - The Sport Event hasn't started yet and is intended to be played according to the schedule (e.g. not POSTPONED or DELAYED)
- POSTPONED - The Sport Event has been POSTPONED do a different day. It will not start now. Postponed sport events CAN have changed start date (if postponing is for shorter time, e.g. up to 48 hours) OR result in scheduling another sport event (with separate ID)
- DELAYED - The Sport Event has been temporarily DELAYED, it will be played the same day, but not at the scheduled time. The delay may be minutes or hours. Delayed sport events retain their original planned start time, but will have different actual start time
- PLAYERS_ON_PITCH - The Players have entered the field of play
- PLAYERS_WARMING_UP - The Players have started warming up
- ABOUT_TO_START - The Sport event is about to start. After the players have completed the warm up and the sport event is due to commence in the next few minutes.
- IN_PROGRESS - The Sport event has begun. Note: Any timeouts or period breaks do not affect this status.
- INTERRUPTED - The game has been INTERRUPTED by an unseen event outside the normal sport flow.  eg Loss of power in the venue
- ABANDONED - The game has stopped and will NOT restart
- ENDED - The game has FINISHED (and Overtime has NOT been played) eg the clock is at 0 at the end of the last period
- ENDED_AFTER_OT - The game has FINISHED (and Overtime HAS been played) eg the clock is at 0 at the end of the last overtime period
- CONFIRMED - The game has ended and all data has been confirmed as correct.
- PROTESTED - The team is protesting the result.

sport_event_status.title: AmericanFootball.SportEventStatus
sport_event_status.description:
Lifecycle status of an American Football sport event. Statuses cover normal progress and exceptional outcomes.
- NOT_STARTED - The American football sport event hasn't started yet (e.g. not POSTPONED or DELAYED).
- CONFIRMED - The American football sport event is officially confirmed to take place as scheduled.
- POSTPONED - The American football sport event has been POSTPONED to a different day. It will not start now.
- DELAYED - The American football sport event is expected to start, but has been temporarily DELAYED. It will still be played on the same day, but not at the scheduled time. The delay may be minutes or hours. Delayed sport events retain their original planned start time, but will have a different actual start time.
- PRE_GAME - Pre-game activities are in progress (e.g. introductions, coin toss, final checks). The American football sport event is imminent, but the game has not officially started.
- IN_PROGRESS - The American football sport event has begun and is ongoing (any regular and/or overtime periods). Note: halftime, timeouts, quarter breaks, and official stoppages do not change this status.
- INTERRUPTED - The American football sport event has been INTERRUPTED by an exceptional event outside the normal sport flow (e.g. severe weather, venue power loss, safety issue). The match may resume later.
- ENDED - The American football sport event has finished normally and has a final result (including any overtimes if played).
- ABANDONED - The American football sport event has started but has been terminated early and will NOT resume.

Lifecycle status of a Counter Strike sport event. Statuses cover normal progress and exceptional outcomes.
- NOT_STARTED - The game hasn't started yet and is intended to be played according to the schedule.
- ABANDONED - The game has been permanently abandoned and will NOT be resumed (e.g. event cancelled mid-map).
- INTERRUPTED - The game started but has been temporarily INTERRUPTED by an unseen event outside the normal sport flow (e.g. technical issue) but will resume later. 
- WALKOVER - The game was awarded to one competitor due to the other competitor not participating (forfeit/no-show).
- RETIRED - The game ENDED due to a competitor retiring during play (e.g. unable to continue); the remaining competitor is awarded the win.
- IN_PROGRESS - The game is currently being played.
- FINISHED - The game has completed normally and a final result is available.
- DELAYED - The Sport Event has been delayed but will still be played on the same date
- POSTPONED - The Sport Event has been postponed to a later date and time
- CANCELLED - The Sport Event has been cancelled and will not be played

data.description: The message payload. It is encoded into a media format which is specified by the datacontenttype attribute (e.g. application/json), and adheres to the dataschema format when those respective attributes are present.

post.description:
This endpoint is used to send a bet settlement message.

### Important information 
- If something happens in a sport event that defines the outcome, your system should send a bet settlement message that contains information about the outcome of bets.
- Possible outcomes:
  - `result`: WON and no `void_factor` - Won entire bet.
  - `result`: LOST and no `void_factor` - Lost entire bet.
  - `result`: VOID and `void_factor`:1 - Refund entire bet.
  - `result`: VOID and `void_reason` - Refund entire bet.
  - `result`: WON and `void_factor`:0.5 - Refund half bet and win other half.
  - `result`: LOST and `void_factor`:0.5 - Refund half bet and lose other half.
- The second subsequent settlement for the same market line is prohibited. If you want to re-settle the market line - send a rollback settlement instead and then a new settlement if needed. 

 **You can find examples of such messages in the `examples` tab.**

allOf.title: CloudEvent
allOf.description:
CloudEvents Specification JSON Schema
See more at https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/v1.0.2/cloudevents/spec.md

id.description:
Identifies the message. Producers MUST ensure that source + id is unique for each distinct message.
If a duplicate message is re-sent (e.g. due to a network error) it MAY have the same id.
Consumers MAY assume that messages with identical source and id are duplicates.

source.description:
Reference: https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/v1.0.2/cloudevents/spec.md#source-1

Producers MUST ensure that `source` + `id` is unique for each distinct message. In S3P, the `source` property is defined this way:

`/<Producer>/<Integration>[:<Version>]/<Sport>/<CoverageId>/<Instance>`

- Producer - a string assigned by SR to an S3P producer. For internal SR services, the `service-key` must be used, e.g. `compsol`, `ld`, `pet` etc.
- Integration - a string provided by the producer indicating the name of the integration to S3P. This may be the name of the product etc. It should be short and contain no spaces, e.g. `dc`, `igp`, `clsplus`.
- Version - an optional string provided by the producer indicating the version of the integration, e.g. `1.0.1`.
- Sport - a string (defined as part of S3P) giving the name of sport or business domain (betting) for which data is being sent, e.g. `basketball`, `cricket`, `football`, `table-tennis`, `betting`.
- CoverageId - This is the unique identifier of the coverage being provided. If the producer does not internally have a coverageId to include, this field should be set to `1`. If the producer knows a coverageId IS in use, but doesn't know what it is, then this field should be set to `0`.
- Instance - a string provided by the producer giving an instance identifier for the producer of the data. For a producer like CV, this could be a particular server or process identifier, for human entered data this could also be an individual scout identifier. Remember to also include this information in the _coverage_ message.

specversion.description:
The version of the CloudEvents specification which the message uses.
This enables the interpretation of the context.
Compliant message producers MUST use a value of 1.0 when referring to this version of the specification.

type.description:
Describes the type of message related to the originating occurrence.
Often this attribute is used for routing, observability, policy enforcement, etc.
The format of this is producer defined and might include information such as the version of the type.

datacontenttype.description:
Content type of the data value. Must adhere to RFC 2046 format.

Compressed data is ALWAYS sent in the _data_base64_ property. The _data_ property is omitted (https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/v1.0.2/cloudevents/formats/json-format.md).

Data sent in compressed format MUST always be a valid json object.

The _datacontenttype_ header indicates the type of compression being used. The field should be of the form `application/` followed by the type of compression (eg _gzip_). When compressed data is not being sent, the _datacontenttype_ header is optional (defaulting to `application/json`). If you are sending compressed data in the _data_base64_ header then the datacontenttype is REQUIRED.

While this may expand in the future, as of now, the only valid value for this is `application/gzip` with the compression being performed with the gzip algorithm.

dataschema.description:
Identifies the JSON schema that data adheres to.
This can be used for JSON Schema validation with tools such as https://ajv.js.org/ or https://github.com/eclipse-vertx/vertx-json-schema.

subject.description:
This property represents the ID of the subject of the message.

`entity:identifier`

Currently, S3P supports these `entities`:

- sport_event
- season
- competition
- competitor
- person

`identifier` is the identifier as given by the producer, so something like `sport_event:sr:match:123` is also valid.
For some scenarios, multiple subjects may need to be given. Eg statistics for a competitor in a competition. In these situations a comma separated list of identifiers should be given.

time.description:
Timestamp of when the message was generated. Must adhere to RFC 3339.
Timestamps related to the data payload have their own properties, and this property only reflects when the message was generated.

data_base64.description: Base64 encoded message payload. Must adhere to RFC4648.

sequence.description:
Value expressing the relative order of the message. This enables interpretation of data supersedence.
See more at https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/v1.0.2/cloudevents/extensions/sequence.md#sequence-1
For Integer sequence types the sequence must be consecutive and begin at 1.

sequencetype.description:
Specifies the semantics of the sequence attribute.
See more at https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/v1.0.2/cloudevents/extensions/sequence.md#sequencetype

traceparent.description:
Contains a version, trace ID, span ID, and trace options as defined in [section 3.2](https://w3c.github.io/trace-context/#traceparent-header)
See more at https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/v1.0.2/cloudevents/extensions/distributed-tracing.md#traceparent

tracestate.description:
a comma-delimited list of key-value pairs, defined by [section 3.3](https://w3c.github.io/trace-context/#tracestate-header).
See more at https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/v1.0.2/cloudevents/extensions/distributed-tracing.md#tracestate

action.description:
In some S3P domains like Event and Commentary, there is a need for updating and deleting existing entities.
This can be achieved by using the `action` property inside the `data` property of the CloudEvent with the values:

- `ADD` - If the entity is new
- `UPDATE` - If the entity is being updated
- `DELETE` - If the entity is being deleted

The values for a specific entity can only change in the following order:

- `ADD` → `UPDATE` → `DELETE`
- `ADD` → `DELETE`

An event cannot be _undeleted_ by sending an action value of `UPDATE`.

Content type of the data value. Must adhere to RFC 2046 format.

Compressed data is ALWAYS sent in the _data_base64_ property. The _data_ property is omitted (https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/v1.0.2/cloudevents/formats/json-format.md).

action.title: Action
action.description:
In some S3P domains like Event and Commentary, there is a need for updating and deleting existing entities.
This can be achieved by using the `action` property inside the `data` property of the CloudEvent with the values:

- `ADD` - If the entity is new
- `UPDATE` - If the entity is being updated
- `DELETE` - If the entity is being deleted

The values for a specific entity can only change in the following order:

- `ADD` → `UPDATE` → `DELETE`
- `ADD` → `DELETE`

An event cannot be _undeleted_ by sending an action value of `UPDATE`.

boundary.description: The value of boundaries scored. Generally used in context of cricket.

competitor1_goals.description: The number of goals scored by competitor 1

competitor.description: The name of the competitor

hole.description: The number or instance of a hole in a match. Used in context of golf

inning.description: The number or the instance of the inning. Used in bat & ball sports like cricket, baseball

kill.description: The number or the instance of a kill inning. Used in E-sports.

lap.description: The number or the instance of a lap. Used in athletic or motor sports.

map.description: The instance of a map. Used in E-sports

penalty.description: The number or instance of penalty

pitch.description: The number or instance of pitch. Used in bat & ball sports.

play.description: The number or instance of play. Used in sports like American Football

region.description: Regional scope for the settlement of the market.

round.description: Refers to the number of or an instance of a round. A round is a stage in a competition

server.description: Refers to the player serving for the game. Used in racquet sports.

session.description: Refers to the number of or an instance of a session. A session is a period of play. Used in sports like cricket

stop.description: The number or instance of a stop. Used in motor sports

timeout.description: The number or instance of a timeout.

to_frame.description: The instance of a frame. Used in conjunction with specifier "from_frame" to refer to two different frames in a market

touchdown.description: The number or instance of a touchdown. Used in sports like American Football & Rugby.

turnover.description: The number or instance of a turnover. Used in sports like Basketball, American Football & Rugby.

visit.description: The number or instance of a visit. A single visit or turn to the board gives the player the chance to throw three darts. Used in sports like darts.

variant.description: The variant of the event. Used in markets where set of outcomes is defined by specific variant.

end.description: Refers to the number of or an instance of an end. An end is a stage in a competition in Bowls

frames.description: The number of frames. A frame refers to a single game in the match. Used in context of cue sports like snooker

games.description: This specifier refers to a number of games. Like x games in Tennis

goals.description: The number of goals in a match

group.description: Refers to a group in a tournament.

innings.description: The number of innings. Used in bat & ball sports like cricket, baseball

matchday.description: Refers to the day in an event.

points.description: Refers to the number of points in the match.

position.description: Represents the position in a league. A position shows where each team ranks in their conference or division.

run_instance.description: Refers to a specific run in a sport. A run is a passage of play in certain sports like Skiing

runs.description: The number of goals in a match. Runs here refer to the score & is used in games like cricket

score_number.description: The number or instance of a score. This is represented numerically. Used in sports like darts, ice hockey

selected_number.description: This indicates the number that has been selected. Used in context of betting games like lottery.

team.description: Refers to a particular team who are part of a match/event. Currently used in "Formula 1"

terms.description: Each-way fraction that is relevant for calculating the payout.

ups.description: Used in spread betting. This specifier is used to represent the score beyond (ups) a certain threshold

winners.description: Represents the number of winners in a game. Used in sports where multiple teams or individuals are participating in the game.

xth.description: The specifier is being used as a variable to refer to a certain incident in a match. Its currently being used in E-sports, Snooker & Darts.

rally.description: Refers to a specific rally in a sport. A rally is the period during which the ball is in play in sports like Table Tennis.

count.description: Refers to the number of a certain event in a match. For example, the number of assists, shots, etc. in a soccer match.

xup.description: Refers to the number of a certain event in a match. For example, the goal advantage in soccer match.

- This is sent when a bet made on a particular market needs to be cancelled and refunded due to an error (which is different to a bet-settlement/refund).

`/<Producer>/<Integration>[:<Version>]/<Sport>/<CoverageId>/<Instance>`

- Sport - a string (defined as part of S3P) giving the name of sport or business domain (betting) for which data is being sent, e.g. `basketball`, `cricket`, `football`, `table-tennis`, `betting`.
- CoverageId - This is the unique identifier of the coverage being provided. If the producer does not internally have a coverageId to include, this field should be set to `1`. If the producer knows a coverageId IS in use, but doesn't know what it is, then this field should be set to `0`.

This endpoint allows you to create a new webhook subscription to receive callback notifications from Sportradar.

### Important information

**This is a critical part of the integration process.** You must ensure that:
- Your webhook endpoint is accessible and reachable from Sportradar servers
- Your endpoint maintains high availability and responds within acceptable timeouts
- Your endpoint is properly secured
- Your endpoint remains healthy to receive real-time notifications
- **If you have a firewall, please whitelist the following IPs:**
  - 18.157.220.30
  - 18.159.91.46
  - 3.68.21.74

**Notification Types**

Your system will receive the following notification types:

**validation_failure** - This notification is sent when Sportradar receives data from your system that fails validation checks:
- Invalid data format or schema violations
- Missing required fields
- Invalid field values or constraints
- Incorrect IDs
- You must:
  1. Use these notifications to identify data issues in your integration

**market_deactivation** - This notification is sent when markets are automatically deactivated due to:
- No Odds/Heartbeat messages received within the required 5-second timeframe
- Use these notifications to monitor the health of your odds feed and take immediate corrective action
- You must:
  1. Immediately respond with an additional Odds Changes message, containing all your currently active markets.
  2. Check on your side why is that the market got deactivated. 

 **You can find examples for each notification under `Response` -> `Examples`. Please be aware, that those are not actual responses from this endpoints - those are example payloads. You will receive similar notifications from us.**

This endpoint allows you to update an existing webhook subscription configuration.

**Important Information**

**Maintaining webhook health is critical for integration success.** When updating your subscription, ensure that:
- The new webhook endpoint URL is accessible and reachable from Sportradar servers
- Your endpoint maintains high availability and responds within acceptable timeouts
- Any authentication or security changes are properly configured
- Your endpoint remains healthy to continue receiving real-time notifications
- **If you have a firewall, please whitelist the following IPs:**
  - 18.157.220.30
  - 18.159.91.46
  - 3.68.21.74
